theme: Indus-script texts found outside South Asia
question: Do Indus-script texts found in Mesopotamia, the Gulf, Iran and Central Asia follow South Asian sign-sequence statistics, and is any deviation larger than regional variation inside South Asia?
outcome: 28 West Asian objects: mean u 0.770 (0.660-0.866), excess 2.11 bits per transition, p at the 1/20,000 floor; round seals 0.870 (0.776-0.945). South Asian regions 0.49-0.57; all four regional differences exclude zero. South Asian round seals 0.704 (0.531-0.872); foreign-minus-South-Asian round 0.165 (-0.026 to 0.357). Central Asian square seals 0.403. Common signs in unusual orders: 3 of 22 foreign texts end with W740 against 34.9% of comparators.
challenge: Small subgroup sizes, transcriptions from published drawings, incomplete join to Laursen's seal numbers, and several rival accounts (another language, names, pseudo-writing, genre, date) predict the same statistic.
remedy: Frozen protocol with hashes, damage-matched comparators, eight sensitivities, independent verifier (22/22 checks).
retry_when: Plate-checked transcriptions of the Gulf-type seals, Laursen's Table 1 joins, or dated contexts for South Asian circular seals become available.
